b:
It was
a dense
forest

And I
was caught there
alone

A dark forest
where not even my shadow
came with me

Family,
those close to me,
dropped away
one by one

Many forgot
that I was lost,
and that I had ever been

I can hear
my own
heartbeat

No one hears
my heart's
cry for help

As fear
wrapped around
half my body,

loneliness,
emptiness
and sorrow
became tears in my eyes

I questioned
and mocked
my birth
and my existence

Because I had become a coward
I did not know how
to kill

A few moths
gave light
now and then

Holding on to them
I came out
of the spreading forest

Some hearts
gathered
around me

They made me
fly
in the wide sky

That
spreading
forest
today
is only
a comma

Many
were caught in worse trouble than me,
in still other forests

Before them
my pain was
like a veil of mist

With so many
around me,
I was the only one
who had crowned himself
with loneliness

When I understood that,
I too
was born anew

Hands reached out:
"This is the world"

Holding on tight
I began to wander

On sleepless nights,
for long
walks,
a few feet
for company

The things I had given up
saying "I can't"
they told me
to try

And the trying
works

Beyond
my circle
I make
a round
of the sky

until
the sky
is within reach

Beautiful relationships
built on love
alone as their foundation

They
are wonderful

Among those
who say
I have changed,

a crowd
that celebrates
that I
have become myself

Tomorrow
another
forest
is waiting
for me

Even if it is
a graveyard,
I will face it

with memories
time cannot erase
and with friendships
without guile
note: The title is a phrase from Abhirami Bhattar's hymn to the goddess Abhirami, which asks for, among other blessings, "a friendship that knows no guile".
